maia: Heads up — saw a perf regression on a small canary after the SM95 rollout. latency for seq128 jumped ~18% on the default kernel path. details below, can someone triage?

vikram: oh no, which workload? encoder-only or decoder?

maia: decoder-heavy chat model. reproduces locally on a single A100-sm95 node with driver 545. logs: `kernel_route: chosen=generic_tf32_v2, fallback=sm95_tc_bf16` and `kv_cache_hits=0.86` — interestingly, we used to pick `sm95_tc_bf16_fastpath` before.

sam: do we have the hw-detect fingerprint for that host? last time a subtle BIOS/PCI topology quirk changed tensor core availability hints.

maia: pasted the probe snippet output: ```hw_probe: sm_major=9 sm_minor=5 tc_count=4 bf16_support=true fp8_partial=false quirks=[pci_mps_lane_swap]```

daria: pci_mps_lane_swap sounds familiar — it triggers our conservative kernel gating which disables the FP8/TC fused kernels. Might be the policy change in the sniffing logic from yesterday.

sam: quick checklist: 1) confirm driver exposes TF32/TensorCore ops, 2) check runtime's cap flags mapping (we recently added a `fp8_partial` tri-state), 3) check sequence-length heuristic: maybe seq128 now maps to different kernel because perf model weights changed.

maia: i ran a microbench: ```microbench --seq 128 --batch 8 --iters 200
chosen_kernel: generic_tf32_v2
latency_p50: 62.1ms
latency_p90: 84.7ms
kv_cache_effective_hit_ratio: 0.86```

benchbot: perf-run queued (id: pr-3127). compare baseline 1690000000 -> will post diffs. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

vikram: i grepped the commit that touched capability flags — looks like we flipped `prefer_tc_on_sm9x` default to false for stability. might be overly conservative.

daria: if the quirk list contains pci_mps_lane_swap we intentionally avoid fused TC kernels because we saw sporadic correctness flakiness. but that should be limited to FP8 kernels; BF16/TC fastpath should still be allowed.

maia: exact diff from today's binary: ```- prefer_tc_on_sm9x = true
+ prefer_tc_on_sm9x = false  # fallback for edge boards```

sam: hypothesis: the new default plus the lane_swap quirk changed the capability mask to drop the bf16_fastpath bit, so routing selects generic_tf32. easy reproduction: flip prefer_tc_on_sm9x back and re-run microbench.

maia: testing now locally with env override: `REDWOOD_CAP_PREFER_TC_ON_SM9X=1 ./runtime`

benchbot: perf-diff complete: p50 delta -9.5% when override set, p90 delta -8.1%. full artifact: https://internal.redwood/perf/pr-3127/diff

vikram: confirms hypothesis. We need a middle ground: keep conservative default but allow BF16 fastpath when driver query indicates bf16 atomic ops stable. maybe add a secondary probe that runs a tiny fused BF16 kernel sanity check on startup.

sam: agree. proposal: on-capprobe add quick smoke: compile/run fused-bf16-kernel(size=64) and validate checksum within threshold. If pass -> set `bf16_fastpath_allowed`. fallback remains for fp8.

daria: also check KV-cache behavior — microbench shows hit_ratio 0.86 which is normal for chat but the routing change may increase KV copy overhead if chosen kernel doesn't support layered KV prefetch. We should log `kvcache_mode` chosen per request for a few minutes.

maia: created a small patch to re-enable prefer_tc_on_sm9x behind smoke test. pushed branch `hwprobe/sm95-bf16-smoke`. running cluster canary now.

ops-bot: canary deploy started -> canary-group: sm95-pool-a (10 nodes). will report after 15m.

vikram: nice. follow-up: add telemetry metric `capprobe.sm95.smoke_pass` + `route.chosen_kernel.{name}` so we can correlate regressions faster.

sam: also add a one-off job to re-run perf matrix for seq lengths [64,128,256] after canary, to ensure no regressions at other seqlens.

maia: thanks all — I'll watch canary metrics and open a follow-up if we need a rollback. :thumbsup:
